title: SSE interruption: snapshot reconciliation and consumer-visible resume token
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Over the past 72 hours we received 3 customer escalations (one Hosted, two Dedicated) reporting abrupt end-of-streams during long-running SSE responses. Symptoms include: client gets an unexpected stream end with final token missing, or a duplicated final token after client-side reconnects. Some customers observe recovered output with small token gaps; others see truncated replies requiring re-issuing the whole request. Impacted workloads are long-context completions (>2048 tokens) and chat sessions with client-side cancellation and HTTP proxy timeouts.

Observed behavior and hypothesis: Preliminary traces show worker A producing tokens up to Tn, then an internal session transition marks the session CLOSED before the final checkpoint is persisted to durable metadata. If the fronting edge (LB/nginx/proxy) closes the TCP/TLS connection due to idle/timeout while the model is finishing its final flush, the client receives an abrupt termination and the server never records the final sequence number. On reconnection the resume path falls back to a fresh request or naively resumes from the last known session marker, causing duplication or gaps. Root cause appears to be a race between final token flush + checkpoint persistence and connection termination/worker handoff.

Goals: 1) eliminate customer-visible truncation/duplication on cancellation or connection tear-down; 2) provide a deterministic and idempotent resume primitive for clients; 3) improve telemetry to make incidents reproducible and diagnosable.

Proposed fixes (implementation plan):
- Durable finalization handshake: introduce a short control event (server-control:finalized) that is emitted only after the final token(s) are flushed and the server has persisted a final_checkpoint_id. The server must ensure checkpoint persistence is acknowledged before the HTTP/SSE connection is allowed to close.
- Resume token in-stream: include a compact resume token in each SSE control event that encodes the committed checkpoint id and last-confirmed-token-index. Clients will be able to present this token to request a deterministic resume from that exact position.
- Idempotent rehydration server-side: on resume requests, worker rehydration must be idempotent (detect duplicate committed checkpoints and replay guard) to avoid emitting duplicate tokens.
- Edge/backpressure hardening: coordinate with infra to add a short grace window (configurable, default 250ms) to LB drain/idle-close behavior for SSE endpoints while finalization is outstanding. Provide a per-customer toggle for Dedicated/Private instances to opt into conservative drain windows.
- Telemetry and tracing: add a new metric sse_unexpected_termination_rate and a span-level event finalization_persist_ack to traces. Surface session lifecycle events in Console (per-session timeline) for customers with advanced debug retention.
- SDK changes and guidance: update official JS/Go SDKs to (a) expose resume token and a resume() helper, (b) retry transparently on transient edge closes using resume() within configurable timebound, and (c) default to conservative reconnect backoff to avoid duplicate replays.

Tests and QA:
- Integration harness: extend integration harness to simulate abrupt TCP close at configurable offsets (at token boundaries, mid-token, during final flush) and assert no data loss or duplication when resume token is used.
- Fault injection in staging: run chaos test where 1% of SSE connections are torn down near-finalization for 48h and validate success criteria.
- Canary: staged rollout behind a feature flag. Start with an internal canary (10% traffic) then 50% then 100% over 24 hours while watching sse_unexpected_termination_rate and customer-reported tickets.

Rollout and mitigation:
- Immediate mitigation (hotfix): deploy a workerside short hold that blocks connection close for up to 500ms if there is unacknowledged finalization work. This is toggleable per-cluster and documented as emergency mitigation for escalations.
- Medium-term (this ticket) implement full durable finalization + resume token + SDK changes.

Observability and post-release checks:
- Add dashboards: per-release small-chart for sse_unexpected_termination_rate, per-region spike alerts, and session timeline viewer in Console.
- Post-release sanity runbook: when customer reports truncation, collect resume token and trace id, use server-side session timeline to validate checkpoint persistence and return reconstructed transcript to customer where possible.

Customer communications:
- Outreach: notify impacted customers with a technical summary & expected timeline and offer emergency mitigation on Dedicated/Private instances.
- KB article: publish an article "How to resume interrupted Hosted SSE responses" with SDK examples and recommended backoff settings.

Why this is different from recent SSE tickets: This change focuses on introducing a committed checkpoint handshake and a consumer-visible resume token rather than only improving reconnect heuristics or checksum reconciliation. The intent is to provide a deterministic primitive for clients and operators to rely on, which reduces reliance on complex server-side heuristics that have produced inconsistent outcomes across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.

2026-03-11 Luca Moretti: Reproduced locally with proxy idle-close at model flush. Confirmed race between persist checkpoint and connection close. Implemented an experiment that delays close by 400ms and saw successful finalization in 98% of trials.

2026-03-12 Priya Shah (SRE): Infra can add a 250ms grace for SSE endpoints via LB config. We need a per-customer toggle for Dedicated. Will schedule change for this week's infra deploy window if approved.
2026-03-12 Mei Chen (SDK): Will add resume token helpers to JS/Go SDKs. ETA for PR: 2026-03-16. Will include examples for how to surface resume token in the streaming callback.

2026-03-13 Luca Moretti: Implementation plan documented above. Starting work on server control event and persistence ack. Marking as In Progress. Blocking: final schema for resume token (security review for token content).
2026-03-13 Security Team: Guidance: resume token must not contain raw PII or secrets. Use HMAC of checkpoint id + short nonce if needed. Security review required before GA.
